transcript_latin_reason: Not available. These calls were transcribed with Prisma's 'codemix' format only (Devanagari and Latin mixed, as the service returned it). A Latin-letter copy needs the service's own transliteration, which was not requested, and no transliteration has been invented here.

uncle_lines.text: <coughs> Haan ji boliye beta, main sun raha hoon.
Police? CBI? Arre baap re, maine toh kuch galat nahin kiya.
Achha, ye likha: 8 2 6. Aage ka phir se boliye beta?
Haan, 0 0 0, 0 3... bas yahin tak likha. Baaki dobara bataiye.
Main pensioner hoon beta, par kar dunga. Kis account mein bhejun?
Mujhe sunai kam deta hai, account number thoda dheere bataiye na beta.

capture.note: While Uncle's voice played, the microphone audio sent to the speech service was silenced, so nothing the caller said during those seconds is in the transcript.

disclosure.policy: Uncle is an automated agent and never says he is a person. A sincere 'are you an AI?' gets the honest answer at once when the call shows little evidence of a scam; with strong evidence he deflects up to twice in character, then answers honestly. This is the project's own policy, not a legal opinion.

ending.detail: The call page's Hang up ended the call. The log cannot say who pressed it; in staged calls the person playing the caller sits at the same computer.

limitations: Staged, role-played call; it says nothing about real scammers.
The transcript is the speech service's codemix text as received. Digits and words can be misheard; items with needs_confirmation true were not confirmed by the caller.
Intel values are as heard. A value that is a piece of a longer one of the same kind is flagged possibly_part_of, not merged.
Times are seconds from the start of the call as measured by the server.
